title: Same Four Beats, Different Performance
description: Each block marks a completion window; blank columns expose initial latency or stalls, while block spacing reveals sustained throughput.

phases.name: B1 done
phases.description: The first completion follows the initial address phase and its data phase.

phases.name: B2 done
phases.description: Once full, the pipeline completes one beat every cycle.

phases.name: B3 done
phases.description: Sustained throughput remains one beat per cycle.

phases.name: B4 done
phases.description: The final completion remains adjacent to the previous beat.

phases.name: B1 done
phases.description: The extra blank column shows a wait state increasing first-beat latency and freezing the next address.

phases.name: B2 done
phases.description: The pipeline briefly returns to one beat per cycle.

phases.name: B3 done
phases.description: Two blank completion windows reveal additional wait cycles reducing average throughput.

phases.name: B4 done
phases.description: The last beat cannot complete until the earlier stall clears.

phases.name: S1 done
phases.description: The slave pays its setup penalty before the first isolated completion.

phases.name: S2 done
phases.description: A new independent address pays the setup penalty again, leaving two blank cycles.

phases.name: S3 done
phases.description: No burst context is available for prefetch or sequential optimization.

phases.name: S4 done
phases.description: The fourth completion arrives far later than in either burst case.

annotations.message: Latency is still two phases, but throughput is now one completed beat per cycle.
Every HREADY-low cycle delays both the current data phase and the following address phase.
Independent transfers can repeatedly pay slave setup cost that a declared burst avoids.
